text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak says deadlock or tension in the peace process hurt the region's peoples, including Israel. It is high time for the Arab world to set up an effective common market, starting with a free-trade zone, he adds during a meeting with university presidents.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will chair the privatisation committee tomorrow to discuss the offer of 34 state-owned firms for sale to the public.
- French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine will visit Egypt within the coming weeks.
- Chairman of the official General Authority for Investment, Ibrahim Fawzi, says that 152 new firms, with a total capital of 1.342 billion pounds ($400 million), were set up between May and August.

- The military prosecutor's office refers 85 defendants to military court. The 85 leaders of the Jihad militant group are charged with planning to carry out suicide attacks against ministers, police officers, writers and artists.

- Mubarak discusses Arab affairs and bilateral relations in telephone calls with Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, President of the United Arab Emirates, and Bahraini Prime Minister Sheikh Khalifa bin Sulman al-Khalifa.
